requirements.text: The automated diagnostic tool detects and identifies faults in chillers and cooling tower subsystems of HVAC units using sensed data acquired from the unit, unit specifications, unit installation and configuration data, and unit operation data (such as schedules).
The tool will provide the user with a visual indication of faults, descriptive information concerning the faults and their causes, and suggested corrective actions.
The tool will store the results of diagnostics for subsequent retrieval and use.
The tool shall input sensed data in real time from data acquisition devices and the HVAC unit under diagnosis.
The tool shall permit sensed data to be input from an electronic file, though not simultaneously with sensed data from external acquisition hardware.
Sensed data used in or supporting diagnostic analyses shall be saved to permanent storage.
The tool shall monitor performance and operational parameters listed in Table 7 for chillers and cooling towers and identify the specific faults in the specific fault categories listed in the table.
With each fault identified in Table 7, the tool shall associate text describing the possible problem, causes, and a recommended fix.

All stored diagnostic data and sensed data must be encrypted at rest using industry-standard algorithms (e.g., AES-256) and access to these files must be restricted to authorized users via OS-level permissions.

The authentication mechanism must enforce strong password policies, store passwords using salted cryptographic hashes (e.g., Argon2 or bcrypt), and implement account lockout after a maximum of 5 failed attempts.
All data transmitted between the HVAC unit, data acquisition devices, and the diagnostic tool must be encrypted in transit using secure protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2+ or VPN tunnels).
The system shall maintain a rolling 365-day archive of diagnostic results and raw sensed data, with an automated cleanup process for data older than one year.
The system shall process incoming sensed data and update diagnostic status within 60 seconds of data acquisition.
The system shall implement a checksum-based validation for stored data and provide a mechanism to export/import the diagnostic database for backup purposes.
The tool shall process incoming sensed data streams with a maximum latency of [X] seconds and support a throughput of [Y] data points per second per HVAC unit.
The tool shall support the concurrent monitoring and diagnostic processing of at least [N] HVAC units across [M] buildings without degradation in performance.
The tool shall retain diagnostic results and raw sensed data for a minimum of [Z] years, with a storage growth rate not exceeding [W] GB per month.
The tool shall display the diagnostic information window within [T] milliseconds of a user double-clicking a cell in the history window.
